sentences.text: Dated this the 3rd day of November, 2025 Petitioner is the sole accused in SC. No,757/2025 on the file of the Sessions Court, Alappuzha, arising from Crime No.133/2025 of Chengannur Police Station.
The offences alleged against the petitioner are under Sections 376(2)(n), 354A (1)(i) of IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST (PoA) Act.

2. The prosecution case is that the accused, who is not a member of scheduled cast or scheduled tribe, after promising to marry the defacto complainant, who is a member of scheduled cast/scheduled tribe, had sexual intercourse with her and thereafter refused to marry her and thereby he alleged to have committed the aforesaid offence.

3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioner, even if the entire allegations raised against the petitioner are accepted in its face value, the same will not constitute the offences alleged against the petitioner.
Therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceeding against the petitioner.
4. Learned Public Prosecutor strongly opposed the petition.

sentences.text: On a perusal of the FI statement, it can be seen that the defacto complainant was a married lady at the time of the alleged incident.
She was living separately from her husband and she was also a mother of a six year old child.
Her case is that the petitioner promised to marry her and believing his words, she lived along with him as husband and wife and thereafter he refused to marry her.
Therefore, from the statement given by the defacto complainant itself, it can be seen that the relationship between herself and the petitioner was a consensual one.

Since the defacto complainant was a married person at the time of the alleged incident, her claim that she had given consent on the basis of the promise made by the petitioner to marry her, cannot be believed.

6. In the above circumstances, as argued by the learned counsel for the petitioner, the allegations against the petitioner does not make out the offences alleged against him and as such continuation of proceedings against the petitioner further will only be an abuse of the process of the court and as such it is liable to be quashed.
In the result, this Criminal M.C. is allowed.

All further 2025:KER:83002 proceedings against the petitioner in SC. No.757/2025 on the file of the Sessions Court, Alappuzha, arising from Crime No.133/2025 of Chengannur Police Station, stands quashed.

Sd/-
C. PRATHEEP KUMAR, JUDGE sou.
